Title: Logical Sum of NDWI & NDPI Data for Detecting Flooded Houses: A Case of Atbasar Town, 2017
Abstract: In this article, NDWI and NDPI data were considered to detect flooded houses hit by a spring flood in Atbasar town, in 2017. This study used remote sensing data Sentinel-2A and Landsat-8 to compute water radiometric indices and formation binary images. Binary images are flood maps generated by threshold values from NDWI and NDPI data and comprise two classes (legend): water body (black color); non-waterbody (white color). Various water indices data were visually analyzed, and the choice was made to Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) and Normalized Difference Pond Index (NDPI) as better. NDWI and NDPI data of Sentinel-2A and Landsat-8 were fused by logical summation. After that, this result was imposed on GIS data of Atbasar Town to define locations and number of flooded houses.

Title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Convert Code to Another Programming Language
Abstract: This study presents a solution to the problem of automating the conversion of program code between different programming languages using artificial intelligence (AI) technologies This area is becoming increasingly relevant with the development of multilingual projects and the need to integrate existing solutions written in different programming languages. The difficulty of translating code between programming languages lies not only in the syntactic differences between languages, but also in preserving the semantics and logic of the original code. Artificial intelligence can help to recognize patterns and dependencies in the code, which will allow you to more effectively adapt the code to the target language, taking into account its features. The use of machine learning algorithms, in particular neural networks, allows you to develop systems that can learn from code examples and independently improve their conversion algorithms. Such systems analyze the abstract syntax tree (AST) of the code, create intermediate representations, and generate the target code. Various tools and platforms have been developed to simplify this process and increase its accuracy. The process of code transformation with the help of AI is used in many areas, including refactoring existing software, integrating systems written in different languages, and in the educational process, where it can be used to teach students the basics of different programming languages.

The system effectively captures and interprets a diverse range of physical movements, including lateral shifts, crouching, and jumping, seamlessly integrating these actions into the gaming environment. Our findings underscore the potential of this pioneering approach to bridge the gap between sedentary screen-based activities and active physical play, offering a harmonious fusion of electronic gaming and real-world sports. This integration not only serves as a catalyst for children to actively participate in physical exercises but also facilitates the acquisition of essential motor skills, contributing to their overall healthy development. Furthermore, the versatility of this approach extends beyond the realm of children, with potential applications in various contexts involving adults. This research not only propels the concept of gamified physical activity promotion but also holds the promise of reshaping the way individuals of diverse age groups engage with technology to lead healthier lifestyles.

Title: Development of a Security and Monitoring System for Server Equipment Utilizing IoT Technologies

Title: Influence of the State Investment Budget on the Kyrgyz Agricultural Sector Through Data Analysis
Abstract: The purpose of this study is to select and assess factors influencing the gross output of the agricultural sector of Kyrgyzstan, considering the specifics of its agricultural producers. Our ideology is since the core of the agricultural producers of Kyrgyzstan are peasant farms, providing two-thirds of the gross output of the sector, as well as personal subsidiary plots of the population, producing an additional one-third of this product. Methodologically, the work is based on the possibility of constructing a correlation-regression model that allows us to assess the impact of selected factors on the resulting indicator. Modeling and corresponding calculations have shown that in modern conditions the most effective indicators for the gross output of the agricultural sector of Kyrgyzstan are such indicators as per capita income of the population, investments in fixed capital, as well as the state investment program budget. In this connection, the indicator "average per capita income" has the highest positive impact on the result. The analysis methodology we used made it possible to identify the main statistical connections of selected factors with the resulting indicator and created the basis for forecasting their changes and developing appropriate measures to increase the volume of gross output of the country's agricultural sector.

Title: Neural Network Threat Detection Systems for Data Breach Protection
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the development of an effective neural network-based threat detection system aimed at identifying and preventing data leaks. Title: Identifying The Coconut Leaf Disease Using Deep Transfer Learning Approach
Abstract: Coconut is one of the main economic crops in Bangladesh. It is a tree whose every part is useful in one way or another in public life. The leaves, flowers, fruits, stems, and roots of this tree are used as raw materials for various small and large industries, materials for making various delicious foods, delicious drinks, and food for patients. This is the world’s most beautiful tree and is well known and appreciated by all as the ’heavenly tree’. However, it has recently become known that most coconut trees suffer from illnesses that gradually weaken the trees’ health and coconut yield. Pest illnesses and nutrient deficits have an impact on the majority of the tree’s leaves. The main reason is that most of the farmers in our country are unaware. They do not know what kind of measures to take in the case of any disease. They are using pesticides, assuming ancient principles, sometimes benefiting and sometimes counterproductively, and making the farmers poor. As a result, farmers are showing disinterest in coconut cultivation. Our main objective is to increase the viability of coconut leaves and detect problems early on so that farmers can benefit more from the cultivation of coconuts. The study suggests examining diseases and detecting insect attacks and nutritional deficiencies in coconut leaves. This will help grow more coconuts. It is expected that this model will help the agricultural field on both an economic and ecological level. This study focuses on the three coconut diseases: WCLWD Yellowing, WCLWD Flaccidity, and CCI Caterpillars. Three neural networks have been chosen in this study to identify the best model. After evaluating the VGG19, MobileNet v2, Inception v3, and ResNet50 models, the accuracy for a collection of 3166 images was determined to be 96%, 96.02%, 97.77%, and 99.36%, respectively. As a result of this technology, farmers will be able to produce more coconuts, surely bringing about a revolution in the agricultural industry.
Keywords: coconut leaf disease;nutrient deficiency;pest attacks;VGG19;MobileNet v2;Inception v3;ResNet50

Title: Data Caching in Edge Computing: A Survey
Abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) generates ever-increasing data streams, traditional cloud-centric architectures face crippling challenges in network latency, bandwidth consumption, and resource constraints. This paper explores how data caching in edge computing environments emerges as a potent solution, significantly impacting latency reduction, network efficiency, and overall system performance. We comprehensively review the landscape of edge IoT and data caching, analyze caching benefits and complexities, and delve into architectural integration, caching strategies, and algorithms tailored to address specific IoT challenges. Through case studies in chosen application domains, we quantify the performance improvements enabled by effective caching and pave the way for future research exploring novel caching methodologies and optimization techniques in the dynamic world of edge IoT.

Title: Security Risks of ML Models: Adverserial Machine Learning
Abstract: Machine learning has emerged as a transformative technology with diverse applications across various sectors. Despite its widespread adoption, the susceptibility of machine learning algorithms to security threats presents a significant challenge. While conventional security risks at hardware and network levels are well-documented, the unique vulnerabilities of machine learning systems require specialized attention.In this paper, we delve into the critical issue of security risks in machine learning, emphasizing the growing concerns surrounding adversarial attacks. To illustrate the practical implications of these security risks, we present a detailed case study on adversarial attacks. By implementing and analyzing an adversarial attack on image classification models, we demonstrate their detrimental effects on model performance and robustness.Our findings underscore the urgent need for proactive measures to safeguard machine learning systems against security threats. By raising awareness and fostering collaboration between researchers and practitioners, we can pave the way for more secure and resilient machine learning frameworks.

Title: The Role of Learning Analytics in Assessing the Effectiveness of Blended Education: A Case Study of Astana IT University
Abstract: The transformation of higher education has brought new forms and approaches to learning to the forefront, highlighting online and blended learning. With the growing popularity of these new learning formats, questions about their effectiveness have arisen, which can be analyzed using learning analytics data. In the Kazakhstani scientific community, interest in learning analytics is in its infancy, reflected in the lack of publications on this topic. The article discusses blended learning at one of the universities in Kazakhstan, namely Astana IT University. The effectiveness of blended learning is analyzed using several methods to address two main research questions. The article includes a comparative analysis of traditional and blended learning formats at the specified university based on data on the overall academic performance of students in four selected socio-humanitarian disciplines from 2021 to 2023. Educational data were obtained from the Modular Object-Oriented Dynamic Learning Environment (Moodle) system. Additionally, the article presents data from a sociological survey among first-year students regarding their perception of the blended learning format. Furthermore, to search for a Pearson linear correlation between online lectures and academic performance data on the number of interactions students have with online content from the Learn system (Open edX) were extracted and analyzed.

Title: Predicting Oil Recovery Coefficient With Machine Learning Methods on Data Generated From the Buckley-Leverett Model
Abstract: The pursuit of enhancing oil extraction processes is now embracing technological advancements, particularly in machine learning (ML), to address the inefficiencies and environmental challenges inherent in conventional methods. This research explores the use of ML algorithms for accurately predicting the Oil Recovery Coefficient (COR), an essential metric for evaluating the effectiveness of oil extraction strategies. Leveraging synthetic data generated through the Buckley-Leverett model, which incorporates variables such as viscosity, porosity, time, and production rate, this study rigorously assesses five ML models: Linear Regressors, Random Forest Regressors, Extreme Gradient Boosting Regressors, Support Vector Machines, and Artificial Neural Networks. Our findings demonstrate that Artificial Neural Networks and Random Forest Regressors notably excel, with R-squared values reaching 0.99981 and 0.99821, respectively, on test datasets. These achievements highlight the superior predictive precision and dependability of these models in estimating COR, marking a significant advancement over existing prediction techniques. In conclusion, this investigation not only evidences the transformative potential of machine learning in refining oil recovery forecasts.

Title: Enhancing OCR Model Training with Synthetic Data: A Case Study with SROIE Dataset
Abstract: This paper investigates the impact of synthetic data on the training effectiveness of optical character recognition (OCR) models. With the rapid advancement in machine learning, the availability of diverse and extensive datasets has become crucial for developing robust OCR systems. However, the scarcity of annotated real-world data poses significant challenges. This study focuses on performing an OCR task using the SROIE dataset, which presents a real-world challenge due to prevalent issues such as paper and ink corruption, inconsistent lighting conditions, variable fonts, colors, background noise, and imaging distortions. We introduce an approach to generating synthetic data, aiming to mimic those peculiarities. By conducting thorough experiments using the SROIE dataset and a custom synthetic training dataset, we demonstrate substantial improvements in model performance, thereby underscoring the potential of synthetic data in OCR applications.

Title: HRBwSD: Hybrid radial based with standard deviation
Abstract: The problem of class imbalance has become a relevant topic in the field of machine learning, and there are several ways to solve this problem, including oversampling, undersampling, and hybrid algorithms. Title: Statistical analysis of the pecto-intercostal fascial plane block on pain-related outcomes in cardiac surgery
Abstract: Treatment of pain is a primary objective in medical hospitals and various plane blocks are used for this purpose. However, the effect of the pecto-intercostal fascial plane block (PIFPB) in cardiac surgery was not studied systematically. In this work, we conduct a statistical analysis of reported data from different countries. The objective of our study was to evaluate pain reduction after the PIFPB in cardiac surgery. We found two studies that reported slightly different pain scores, namely, pain measured at rest and with movement. The model favors the experimental (bupivacaine, ropivacaine) group over the control (placebo) group in terms of postoperative pain (SMD with 95% CI is –1.29 [–1.68, –0.89], p-value < 0.00001). However, the total length of hospital stay was longer in the experimental group with a mean difference of 1.35 days with 95% CI [1.04, 1.66] and p-value < 0.00001. The model showed no significant difference between groups in opioid consumption. To summarize, PIFPB after cardiac surgery reduces pain intensity scores but results in longer hospital stays. More trials should be done in the future to examine the effect of PIFPB on other medical outcomes.

Title: Development and Research of Phased Array Antenna Control Unit for Educational Purposes
Abstract: The research examined the technology of creating one of the main component of the phased array antenna - the phase shifter control unit. This control unit is designed to operate a phased array antenna model of four emitters for academic purposes. The antenna model includes four emitters, in the circuit of each emitter there are two switches that form the necessary phase shifts. Switches can be changed over in three directions, which allows the formation of three antenna beams. Title: Community structure detection in complex network based on MST and modularity
Abstract: This research introduces a new splitting and merging method to identify community structure in networks. This proposed approach relies on constructing a minimal spanning tree (MST) based on the dissimilarities between nodes in a graph and optimizing the modularity function. The Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a graph is detached by deleting edges with high dissimilarity values between nodes during the splitting phase. Title: Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Forecasting Harvest Data in Kazakhstan
Abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of machine learning algorithms for forecasting harvest data in Kazakhstan. Leveraging extensive datasets spanning over three decades, our research evaluates the performance and predictive accuracy of various algorithms in forecasting potato yields—the predominant crop in the region. Through empirical analysis, Linear Regression, Lasso Regression, and Ridge Regression emerge as top-performing models, exhibiting R^2 scores exceeding 0.95. These linear models effectively capture the complex relationship between weather conditions and agricultural outcomes, offering valuable insights for agricultural planning and decision-making. Additionally, Gradient Boosting and ElasticNet algorithms demonstrate competitive performance, highlighting the potential of ensemble learning techniques in agricultural forecasting. Conversely, Support Vector Regression (SVR) exhibits poor performance in this context, emphasizing the importance of selecting appropriate algorithms tailored to the specific characteristics of agricultural datasets. Overall, our findings underscore the significance of employing advanced machine learning techniques to enhance the accuracy and reliability of harvest forecasts, thereby empowering stakeholders in the agricultural sector to make informed decisions and ensure food security in Kazakhstan.

Title: Analysis of the Transfer Characteristics of Refractive Indices and Nonlinear Effects in Optical Optical Fibers Using the Example of Chromatic Dispersion
Abstract: This article shows the physical basis of dispersion and demonstrates that using a strictly monochromatic laser radiation source for signal transmission in glass fiber is impossible. It was shown that the average dispersion has a negative value, corresponding to the slope of the wavelength curve from the refractive index, and normal dispersion is also shown. Differential changes were taken near the wavelength of 1300 nm, corresponding to the transparency window in the infrared range and widely used in optical telecommunication systems. Considering the fluctuation heterogeneity of the glass fiber structure used in modern systems and the changing gradient refractive index, light waves move in the path at different speeds and arrive at the endpoint at different points in time, creating a time pulse of information transmission. The article contains basic mathematical apparatus - the theory of logarithms, finite and infinitesimal increments, elements of mathematical statistics. The main emphasis is placed on the issues of molecular optics and the interaction of light with different refractive indices of glass fiber.

Title: Candidate Generation for Meal Recommendation System
Abstract: In this paper we overview a recommendation system architecture proposed by Google and adjust it to for our meal recommendation system. Then we conduct an overview on models used for building recommendation systems, as well as a candidate generation for the recommendation system. Title: Cognitive Technologies for Object Detection and Topology of the Environment's Information Space
Abstract: The widespread use of ontologies in various fields makes the task of its automated formation quite relevant. The problems associated with its construction within the framework of Data Science and Advanced Analytics are data integration and high-quality information search. Increasing the efficiency of working with ontology is ensured by the connection of cognitive processes with semantic ones. The difference between the analysis, the results of which are presented in this paper, is the cognitive information technologies of the subject area, cognitive and semantic analysis based on the topology of the information space of the environment, which was carried out for the first time. To form a concept in an intellectual environment, the use of the concept's normalization and its features is defined and substantiated. The construction of ontologies is based on the connection of cognitive processes with semantic ones and actualization - description and identification of cognitive information's sources in intellectual environments of subject areas. An approach to formalizing the representation of an information object is considered. The research as a source of information for further formalization and modeling of the information object representation is carried out. The problems that arise in the process of formalizing and analyzing an information object are identified and described. The main difference of the study is the cognitive-semantic analysis based on the theory of mathematical logic and universal algebra, set algebra, tuple algebra and relational algebra, namely: building on open languages of knowledge representation and relations of information sources - tasks - information units.

Title: Integrated Computer Network Security System: Intrusion Detection and Threat Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms
Abstract: The escalating use of computer networks and associated applications has made cybersecurity a critical concern. This research presents a comprehensive approach to addressing network security issues by developing an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on the dataset from the Security Information and Event Management System (SIEM) using various machine learning algorithms. The study includes a detailed comparison of models such as Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Gusain Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Artificial Neural Networks. The research evaluates the model’s performance across various cyber-security datasets containing multiple categories of cyber-attacks. It evaluates efficiency by utilizing criteria such as accuracy, precision, and recall. By applying a multilevel approach aligned with the latest trends in machine learning, the study aims to facilitate swift and precise threat analysis and response, ultimately enhancing the overall effectiveness of the cybersecurity system. The study is an effective educational resource that introduces IT students to innovative machine learning and cybersecurity ideas. Through the integration of the results into IT curriculum, educators may close the knowledge gap between theory and practical application by offering students real-world experience in addressing cyber threats. This combined emphasis on innovation and education seeks to develop a new generation of IT professionals with the expertise required for enhanced cybersecurity.

Title: Conceptualizing the ICT project management in the sustainability context
Abstract: This paper discusses the roles and opportunities that ICTs play in the pursuit of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It is claimed that the efficient use of digital technologies is possible if the IT project management of sustainability methodology is used. The links and gaps between ISO standards and the SDGs presented. The correlation of ISO standards for project, program, and portfolio management with 17 SDGs investigated. Correlations with SDGs 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, and 16 identified. The contextual analysis of the opportunities for the use of ICTs for the achievement of the SDGs revealed two levels of responsibility in terms of sustainability. Firstly, ICT acts as an accelerator for managing projects and programs in different areas (environmental, economic, and social). Secondly, the high intensity of development of the ICT field itself requires the initiation and implementation of the SDGs in the ICT field itself. It is noted that the development of a methodology for sustainable management of ICT projects can be built by integrating project management standards and establishing a correlation with all SDGs. The integration of sustainability in ICT project management can start with the acceleration of project management processes, followed by improving sustainability competencies.

Title: Gamification Effects on Employee Engagement and Business Process Risk Evaluation
Abstract: This research explores the effectiveness of gamification as a method to boost employee engagement and improve organizational processes. Title: Developing a Kazakh question-answering model: standing on the shoulders of multilingual giants
Abstract: At present, there is a proliferation of AI-powered systems being developed to enable natural language interactions with humans. However, these systems are primarily designed for a limited set of approximately 40 dominant languages, while the majority of the world’s over 7,000 living languages, including Kazakh, are categorized as under-resourced languages that lack cutting-edge AI technologies like Siri, GPT-3, etc. The solution is to leverage state-of-the-art multilingual models, which have recently emerged as vital resources for lowresource languages, facilitating the rapid development of native language models with acceptable quality. This study focuses on the comprehensive evaluation of various multilingual models, including mT5, XLM-RoBERTa, and mDeBERTa with the aim to determine their suitability as donor models for Kazakh question answering. Furthermore, the study addresses the research question of whether large multilingual models genuinely outperform native language models in the task of question answering. Experimental results confirm this superiority and lead to the conclusion that there is no need to train native models from scratch, considering the associated economic and environmental costs.
Keywords: large language models;multilingual models;question-answering;low resource languages;SQuAD

Title: Real Estate Price Management Through Fuzzified Time Impact Factors Using MATLAB: Development Companies’ Approach
Abstract: The profitability of a real estate development company depends on the effective formulation of a marketing strategy that integrates dynamic factors along with static ones in real estate price management. This article explores the fuzzy set theory application using MATLAB for managing the challenges posed by time impact factors, which demonstrate fluctuation during the implementation of various real estate development projects. Evolving consumer preferences, local real estate market conditions, and the construction processes complexness influence these factors. The analysis of Group Impact Factors, influenced by time parameters, discloses trends in real estate prices across different combinations of sale offer exposure periods and construction stages.This article suggests integrating results of MATLAB utilization, specifically Group Impact Factors pseudo-color plots and Time Impact Factors membership function plots, into the real-time formation of development companies' marketing strategies. These tools facilitate a dynamic factors assessment, taking into account not only the expected development project profitability but also the real-time demand for real estate within local markets and individual development projects. Using Time Impact Factors for real estate price formation enhances flexibility, providing not only desired price values but also minimum permissible ones, thereby optimizing price offers and stimulating demand.In conclusion, the authors underline the suitability of fuzzified Time Impact Factors for economic forecasting, risk management, and investment flow optimization in real estate development projects. Proposed MATLAB-based tools and approaches are declared beneficial for development companies in both strategic and tactical planning.

Title: Institutional measurement of structural characteristics of residential real estate markets using the method of cluster analysis
Abstract: The article examines the use of IT technologies and cluster analysis tools to solve the problem of classifying regions of Ukraine according to the level of their institutional development. Recognizing the importance of effective institutional frameworks for economic growth, social stability and governance, the research focuses on using data-driven approaches to assess and classify regional institutional dynamics. Through a combination of data collection, statistical analysis, and machine learning methods, the study aims to provide an understanding of the spatial distribution and characteristics of institutional development in the regions of Ukraine. Using cluster analysis methodologies, such as K-means clustering, the study identifies distinct groups or clusters of regions with similar institutional profiles. Title: Image-Based Dietary Assessment: A Healthy Eating Plate Estimation System
Abstract: The nutritional quality of diets has significantly deteriorated over the past two to three decades, a decline often underestimated by the people. This deterioration, coupled with a hectic lifestyle, has contributed to escalating health concerns. Recognizing this issue, researchers at Harvard have advocated for a balanced nutritional plate model to promote health. Inspired by this research, our paper introduces an innovative Image-Based Dietary Assessment system aimed at evaluating the healthiness of meals through image analysis. Our system employs advanced image segmentation and classification techniques to analyze food items on a plate, assess their proportions, and calculate the meal’s adherence to Harvard’s healthy eating recommendations. This approach leverages machine learning and nutritional science to empower individuals with actionable insights for healthier eating choices. Our four-step framework involves segmenting the image, classifying the items, conducting a nutritional assessment based on the Harvard Healthy Eating Plate research, and offering tailored recommendations. The prototype system has shown promising results in promoting healthier eating habits by providing an accessible, evidence-based tool for dietary assessment.

Title: Use the neural networks in prediction of environmental processes
Abstract: Forecasting environmental phenomena using neural networks has become increasingly popular due to their ability to analyze complex datasets and provide accurate predictions. In this paper, we investigate the application of neural networks in predicting environmental processes, focusing specifically on their use in forecasting greenhouse gas emissions. We examine several types of neural networks, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) such as Simple RNN, LSTM-RNN, and stacked LTSM-RNN, to assess their effectiveness in handling raw data and projecting emissions over different spatial and temporal scales. The study demonstrates that the Simple RNN model is highly accurate in outlier prediction. Moreover, the consistency of results obtained through decision tree construction with those from component and cluster analyses is highlighted. The scientific significance of this study lies in its comprehensive exploration of neural networks' ability to forecast environmental processes, with a specific emphasis on greenhouse gas emissions prediction. The findings suggest that neural networks, particularly recurrent architectures, show promise as powerful tools for monitoring and forecasting environmental changes, offering valuable insights for governmental agencies and environmental initiatives.

Title: STEM education in Poland and Ukraine: exploring the contextual data of the GGG Index
Abstract: The assessment and monitoring of educational attainment in Poland and Ukraine in terms of ensuring gender parity in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) were explored. It is noted that the new educational visions should be based on the acquisition of knowledge in STEM fields and fluency with digital tools. STEM careers are expected to be among the most in-demand in the context of Industry 4.0. The Global Gender Gap Index (GGGI) used to achieve a comprehensive gender analysis. The category subindexes “Educational Attainment” determines the scale of the imbalance between women and men. The retrospective analysis of the transformation of the indicator system for assessing the educational attainment performed. Title: A hybrid approach for a movie recommender system using Content-Based, Collaborative and Knowledge-Based Filtering methods
Abstract: Rapid evolution of information technology has rapidly increased the significance of Internet-generated data. As a result, finding specific information within this vast data landscape has become increasingly challenging for individuals. Recommender systems have emerged as precious tools in response to this challenge, offering assistance in navigating and extracting relevant information from the abundance of available data. As user engagement increases in importance, recommender systems will be considered an integral part of personalized marketing. The most common methods leverage product features (Content-Based), user similarity (Collaborative Filtering), and personal information (Knowledge-based). However, with the increasing popularity of Neural Networks, companies have started experimenting with new Hybrid Recommendation Systems that combine them all. Title: A Comparative Study of Supervised Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques with Feature Selection Methods for Classifying Parkinson’s Disease Based on Speech Impairments
Abstract: This paper compares and analyzes machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques with different feature selection methods for classifying Parkinson’s disease based on a speech impairments dataset. The dataset was explored by various methods to obtain vocal features, including Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Wavelet Transform Features, Vocal Fold Features, and Tunable Q-factor wavelet transform (TQWT). It consists of 754 features and 756 instances. In addition, the study evaluates various classification techniques, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Naive Bayes (NB), Deep Neural Network (DNN), 1D Convolution Neural Network (1D CNN). Additionally, we demonstrated the effectiveness of feature selection techniques, namely Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR), and SelectKBest. Among these, the most notable accuracy and precision were achieved by the KNN algorithm combined with PCA, recording values of 93.43% and 93.45%, respectively. Moreover, the Random Forest (RF) algorithm achieved an outstanding recall rate of 100%

Title: Developing Intelligent Supply Chain System Adopting Lean and Agile Attributes for Construction Projects in Malaysia
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to examine the impact of lean and agile attributes towards triple constraints and develop intelligent supply chains for construction projects in Malaysia. Title: Game-Theory Model of a Two-Level Hierarchical Game with Distributed Control

Title: Using Computer Modeling for Tracking high-order Nonlinear Systems with Time-Delay
Abstract: This paper investigates the challenge of globally practically tracking a class of high-order nonlinear systems with time delay via feedback. The object of study is a nonlinear system, the main goal is to develop a control function that allows you to regulate the output data of the specified nonlinear system using a reference signal. The article publication is distinguished by its scientific novelty due to the study of a system in which the degree of the upper limit of nonlinearity is determined within a continuous interval. The system under examination exhibits a distinctive characteristic, wherein the extent of the upper boundary limitation of nonlinearity is defined within a continuous interval. We propose a customizable and delay-independent tracking controller designed to mitigate the impact of delay time non-linearity. This is achieved by generating a Lyapunov function using a generalized approach that involves incorporating a signum function and a power integrator. Title: Statistical analysis of outcomes of basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation for vertebrogenic chronic low back pain management
Abstract: In the era of office work, many people suffer from chronic low back pain (CLBP). Intra-osseous basivertebral nerve radiofrequency ablation (BVN RFA) is considered a way to treat vertebrogenic CLBP. However, the BVN RFA was not well studied. Using PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library, we found four studies of BVN RFA from the US and performed a statistical analysis of its effect on CLBP. We compared the sample statistics of the studies on pain intensity and LBP-related disability both in pre- and postoperative stages in two groups: treatment and control. Using the RevMan v. 5.4 software, we calculated the mean difference (MD) for each outcome between the groups and constructed forest plots. On a 0-10 pain scale, our results showed the postoperative pain intensity reduction in the treatment group compared to the control group (MD with 95% CI is –1.63 [–2.91, –0.35], p-value = 0.01). There was a considerable improvement in disability index as well (MD with 95% CI is –10.36 [–22.87, 2.14] on a 0-50 scale, p-value = 0.10), but the result was not statistically significant. Our analysis concludes that the intra-osseous BVN RFA is effective in reducing vertebrogenic CLBP, but more randomized controlled trials would be beneficial to study the effect of BVN RFA in more detail.

Title: Enhancing Gameplay Experience Through Reinforcement Learning in Games
Abstract: It is important to improve the game development field since games have great influence on economics and society. One of the ways to enhance game experience is to replace non-playable characters (NPC) by machine learning (ML) agents. During the research initialization phase, there were set null hypothesis, which states that pre-scripted bots are better for games and alternative hypothesis, which states that AI can replace NPC and enhance the game experience for a player.

Title: Mobile Application of Convolutional Neural Networks for Melanoma Classification
Abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most common types of cancer in terms of incidence around the world. Melanoma, in particular, manifests as visible pigmented skin lesions, often a result of sun overexposure. Despite the fact of rapid development of dermatology, delays in diagnosing skin diseases and poor access to their treatment are occurring in modern medicine.Several studies have demonstrated the potential of CNN in developing accurate and noninvasive screening methods for skin cancer. Nowadays, a limited number of mobile applications are identified that involve deep learning for the scanning and screening of skin diseases.This study simultaneously proposes a CNN architecture with a non-standard activation function, as well as presents the results of the proposed CNN model in terms of various metrics, such as accuracy, recall, specificity, precision, and so on. The software development is implemented in the Flutter framework, focusing on the Waterfall model. The key components of the mobile application, including the splash screen, main page, navigation, health-related features, and the "About Us" section, are described.The results of this study demonstrate that the proposed CNN model achieved 81.53% in terms of accuracy. The image augmentation techniques employed contribute to improved model generalization and robustness. By combining the capabilities of CNNs with user-friendly mobile interfaces, individuals can gain easy access to melanoma assessment, promoting proactive healthcare practices.

Title: Hybrid Deep Neural Network for Face Liveness Detection in Real-Time Video
Abstract: This paper presents a novel Hybrid Deep Neural Network approach for enhancing face liveness detection in video sequences, a critical component in safeguarding biometric authentication systems against sophisticated spoofing attacks. Leveraging the strengths of convolutional neural networks for spatial and frequency domain feature extraction the proposed model offers a comprehensive solution to detect and differentiate between live and spoofed face presentations. Utilizing the OULU-NPU dataset, featuring real-world variations and diverse spoofing scenarios, our model was rigorously evaluated across multiple performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The research introduces dynamic thresholding and Grad-CAM visualizations to improve decision-making flexibility and model interpretability, respectively. The results demonstrate the HDNN model's significant performance and adaptability to various attack vectors and environmental conditions, making a significant contribution to the field of biometric security. In addition to advancing face liveness detection technologies, this work paves the way for future investigations into biometric identification systems that are more reliable and effective.

Title: Simulation of motion control of a cylindrical robot manipulator

Title: Intelligent monitoring system based on Atmega microcontrollers in healthcare with stress reduce effect
Abstract: Ensuring the well-being of people is one of the most important responsibilities in modern society. Medical Internet of Things (IoMT) plays a key role in the medical and healthcare fields. This research aims to develop a patient monitoring system using sensors and Arduino platforms, combining hardware and software components. The system includes three main sensors to collect and transmit patient health data to a central server via a network. If an anomaly is detected, the system instantly notifies the doctor with an alarm message. To evaluate the convenience and importance of the system for patients, tests were conducted on 287 people. Patient data included various characteristics such as age, gender, place of residence, hemoglobin concentration, red blood cell count and other data obtained at the last doctor's visit, as well as daily data from Arduino sensors. The use of data in the intelligent part of the system makes it possible to predict the development of cardiovascular diseases and track the progress of the disease, although this requires more research.

Title: Assessing Urbanization Levels Using GeoData: Implications for Kazakhstan Regional Development Planning

Title: Dual-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing with Integrated Spatial and Frequency Analysis Neural Network
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel dual-domain approach for face anti-spoofing, aimed at enhancing the robustness and accuracy of spoofing detection mechanisms. Our model uniquely combines spatial domain analysis with frequency domain insights, employing a two-branch and dual loss neural network architecture that leverages augmented images and their Fourier transforms during the training stage. The EfficientNetV2s pre-trained model serves as the base structure, and an additional component, termed the Fourier head, is inserted into an intermediate layer of the backbone. This component is specifically designed to reconstruct the frequency map of the input image. It helps to capture a comprehensive set of features indicative of spoofing attacks, including textural and color anomalies as well as recurrent patterns not visible in the spatial domain. Tested on the OULU-NPU dataset, our methodology has demonstrated exceptional performance, achieving near state-of-the-art results on most protocols. Thus, our model is capable of accurately distinguishing between genuine and spoofed facial images, thereby confirming the advantage of integrating spatial and frequency domain analyses for face anti-spoofing.

Abstract: This research paper delves into the integration of wearable devices and deep learning techniques to enhance heart disease detection and monitoring. The study highlights the importance of continuous cardiac health assessment and the transformative potential of wearable technology in the healthcare landscape. Our investigation showcases their efficacy in processing intricate physiological data for early heart disease recognition. Key variables such as age, maximum heart rate, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, and various electrocardiography (ECG) metrics are explored as pivotal factors in predicting and comprehending heart disease risk factors. Furthermore, we emphasize the significance of data normalization methodologies and secure data storage solutions to ensure data reliability and accessibility. Correlation analyses elucidate the intricate interplay among these variables, providing valuable insights into their collective influence on cardiac health. As the realm of machine learning and healthcare technology continues to evolve, this research lays a solid foundation for advancing heart disease detection and management, ultimately aiming to enhance patient outcomes and elevate the quality of healthcare delivery.

Title: A Deep Learning for Cardiovascular Diseases Detection on Wearable Devices Data
Abstract: This research paper explores the potential of deep learning techniques in the early detection of cardiovascular diseases using data collected from wearable devices. With the advent of advanced wearable technology, continuous monitoring of physiological parameters, such as heart rate, electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, and physical activity patterns, has become feasible. Leveraging the power of deep neural networks, we investigate the development of predictive models capable of identifying individuals at risk of cardiovascular diseases. The study employs rigorous data preprocessing techniques, encompassing feature extraction and data segmentation, in conjunction with Machine Learning algorithms to enhance model accuracy. Additionally, regularization methods, notably dropout, are harnessed to address challenges posed by diverse datasets. The research envisions the incorporation of data derived from everyday activities to comprehensively assess their impact on heart health, ultimately aiming to proactively alert individuals to deteriorating cardiovascular conditions. The findings presented herein encourage further exploration and innovation in the realm of cardiovascular disease detection, fostering advancements that can enhance public health and well-being.

Title: Regression and Machine Learning Methods for Predicting Human Movements Based on Skeletal Data
Abstract: In recent years, the advancement of computer vision technologies has facilitated the extraction of skeletal data from human movements captured in video sequences. Leveraging this wealth of information, this article explores the application of regression and machine learning methods to predict human movements based on skeletal data. The objective is to develop models that can accurately forecast and understand the dynamics of various human motions.The methodology involves the use of computer vision techniques for skeleton detection and tracking, followed by careful preprocessing of the skeletal data to extract relevant features. These features, representing key aspects of the skeletal structure and motion, serve as inputs to regression and machine learning models. Various algorithms, including linear regression, support vector machines, random forests, and deep neural networks, are employed to learn the intricate relationships between skeletal features and corresponding movements.A crucial aspect of the study is the creation of a comprehensive training dataset that captures diverse human movements. Data augmentation techniques are applied to enhance the variability and robustness of the training set. The trained models are then rigorously evaluated using metrics such as mean squared error to quantify their predictive performance.Results indicate that the proposed regression and machine learning approaches exhibit promising capabilities in predicting human movements. The article discusses the strengths and limitations of different algorithms, highlighting their applicability in various contexts, including virtual reality, augmented reality, security systems, and robotics. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the importance of continuous refinement and adaptation of models to accommodate the complexity and variability inherent in human motion.This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge at the intersection of computer vision and human movement prediction, paving the way for innovative applications in fields such as human-computer interaction, biomechanics, and artificial intelligence. The findings underscore the potential of regression and machine learning methods in enhancing our understanding and prediction of human movements based on skeletal data.
